knowledge:
- key_parameters: groupBy=Specifies the column in metadata to group samples for matching pairs (e.g., "patient" to match treated and control samples from the same patient) ;; sampleColumn=Name of the metadata column containing sample names matching the logCPM matrix column names ;; treatColumn=Name of the metadata column containing treatment information (must be a factor with control as the reference level) ;; database=Specifies the pathway database (e.g., "kegg", "reactome", "wikipathways") ;; species=Specifies the species (e.g., "hsapiens") ;; keyword=Optional keyword to filter retrieved pathways (e.g., "metabolism") ;; NB=Optional parameter to specify the number of permutations (defaults to all possible permuted pairs if not specified) ;; sortBy=Determines how the output is sorted (e.g., "pvalue", "gs_name", "sample") ;; filterBy=Method to filter genes for visualization (e.g., "mean") ;; topGene=Number of top genes to plot ;; mapEntrezID=Data frame mapping Entrez IDs to other identifiers (e.g., gene symbols) ;; colorBy=Variable to color nodes by (e.g., "status", "-log10(p)")
- alternatives: SPIA (Signaling Pathway Impact Analysis) is the underlying algorithm from which sSNAPPY adopts its pathway perturbation scoring approach.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing RNA-seq data with matched/paired samples (e.g., treated vs. control from the same patient) to compute directional pathway perturbation scores at a single-sample level while incorporating pathway topology (gene-gene interactions).
- pitfalls: Row names of the logCPM matrix must be converted to Entrez IDs before running the workflow because retrieved pathway topologies use Entrez IDs ;; The treatment column in the metadata must be a factor, and the control treatment must be set as the reference level (first level) ;; When sample size is small, the total number of possible permuted pairs is small, meaning small p-values cannot be accurately estimated; thus, p-values from normalise_by_permu() should be interpreted with caution ;; If mapping Entrez IDs to gene names in plot_gene_contribution(), genes that fail to map successfully will be omitted from the plot.

workflows.name: single_sample_pathway_perturbation
workflows.intent: Compute single-sample directional pathway perturbation scores, test their significance using sample permutation, perform treatment-level linear modeling, and visualize gene contributions and pathway networks.
input: logCPM_matrix (normalized logCPM matrix with Entrez IDs as row names and sample names as column names)
metadata_df (sample metadata data frame containing sample names, patient/grouping IDs, and treatment factors with control as reference)
workflows.stages: 1. Compute weighted single-sample logFCs (ssLogFCs) using weight_ss_fc() ;; 2. Retrieve pathway topologies using retrieve_topology() ;; 3. Compute raw gene-level perturbation scores using raw_gene_pert() ;; 4. Sum gene-level scores to compute pathway-level perturbation scores using pathway_pert() ;; 5. Generate null distributions of perturbation scores via sample permutation using generate_permuted_scores() ;; 6. Normalize scores and calculate empirical p-values using normalise_by_permu() ;; 7. Perform treatment-level linear modeling using lm() ;; 8. Visualize gene contributions using plot_gene_contribution() ;; 9. Visualize pathway networks using plot_gs_network(), plot_community(), and plot_gs2gene()
workflows.code:
weightedFC <- weight_ss_fc(logCPM_example, metadata = metadata_example, groupBy = "patient", sampleColumn = "sample", treatColumn = "treatment")
gsTopology <- retrieve_topology(database = "kegg", species = "hsapiens")
genePertScore <- raw_gene_pert(weightedFC$weighted_logFC, gsTopology)
pathwayPertScore <- pathway_pert(genePertScore, weightedFC$weighted_logFC)
permutedScore <- generate_permuted_scores(expreMatrix = logCPM_example, gsTopology = gsTopology, weight = weightedFC$weight)
normalisedScores <- normalise_by_permu(permutedScore, pathwayPertScore, sortBy = "pvalue")
fit <- normalisedScores %>% left_join(metadata_example) %>% split(f = .$gs_name) %>% lapply(function(x)lm(robustZ ~ 0 + treatment, data = x)) %>% lapply(summary)
treat_sig <- lapply(names(fit), function(x){ fit[[x]]$coefficients %>% as.data.frame() %>% .[seq_len(2),] %>% dplyr::select(Estimate, pvalue = `Pr(>|t|)` ) %>% rownames_to_column("Treatment") %>% mutate(gs_name = x, FDR = p.adjust(pvalue, "fdr"), Treatment = str_remove_all(Treatment, "treatment") ) }) %>% bind_rows()
plot_gene_contribution(genePertMatr = genePertScore$`kegg.Proteoglycans in cancer` %>% .[, str_detect(colnames(.), "E2", negate = TRUE)], filterBy = "mean", topGene = 10, color = rev(colorspace::divergex_hcl(100, palette = "RdBu")), breaks = seq(-0.001, 0.001, length.out = 100))
p1 <- pathway2plot %>% plot_gs_network(gsTopology = gsTopology, colorBy = "status")
pathway2plot %>% plot_community(gsTopology = gsTopology, colorBy = "status", color_lg_title = "Community")
treat_sig %>% dplyr::filter(FDR < 0.05, Treatment == "R5020") %>% mutate(status = ifelse(Estimate > 0, "Activated", "Inhibited")) %>% plot_gs2gene(gsTopology = gsTopology, colorGsBy = "status", geneFC = top500_FC, mapEntrezID = entrez2name, gsNameSize = 3, filterGeneBy = 0)
